title: Monitoring and alerting
summary: What every production service should show and alert on, so that problems are noticed before customers report them and incidents are quicker to solve.
scope: Services of tier 0 to 2 that run in production. Tier 3 tools and batch jobs are out of scope.

requirements.title: A standard service dashboard
requirements.statement: Each service has a dashboard with request rate, error rate, response time and saturation, named after its service id.
requirements.rationale: During an incident everyone looks at the same four numbers first.
guidance: Generate the dashboard from the template with the process 'Set up monitoring and alerts for a service'.

verification.description: Weekly report of services in the catalogue without a dashboard.

requirements.title: Alerts page for customer impact only
requirements.statement: Alerts that page someone fire on what customers notice - errors and slow responses - not on causes such as high CPU.
requirements.rationale: On-call engineers who are woken for nothing stop trusting the alerts.
guidance: Page on error rate and response time.
Send cause alerts (CPU, disk, queue length) to the team channel instead of paging.

verification.description: Reviewed by the Observability team on every alert change.

lookFor: A paging alert on CPU, memory or disk usage
An alert with no 'for' duration, which pages on every spike

requirements.title: Trace id in every log line
requirements.statement: Logs carry the trace id of the request, so that one customer request can be followed across services.
requirements.rationale: Without it an incident across several services takes hours to piece together.
guidance: Use the logging setup of the platform library; it adds the trace id.

lookFor: A new HTTP handler or consumer that logs without the request context

requirements.title: Every paging alert links to a runbook
requirements.statement: Each alert that pages someone links to a short runbook: what it means, what to check first and how to escalate.
requirements.rationale: At 3 a.m. the on-call engineer may not know the service well.
guidance: Add a runbook_url annotation to each paging alert.
End every runbook with a link to the incident process.

verification.description: Alert rules without runbook_url are reported in the alert repository.

lookFor: A paging alert rule without a runbook_url annotation

requirements.title: Service level objectives
requirements.statement: Teams may define service level objectives and alert on how fast the error budget is used instead of on fixed thresholds.
requirements.rationale: Error budget alerts page less often and for the right reasons.
